newsitem.title: HAITI: Preval plays down Haiti role for U.S. agents.
newsitem.headline: Preval plays down Haiti role for U.S. agents.

text.p: Haitian President Rene Preval played down the presence of U.S. security officers at the National Palace on Tuesday, restating the official position that they came to Haiti to train a local security force.
"They are here to reform and professionalize the security team here," Preval told reporters after meeting with Canadian Minister of International Cooperation Pierre Pettigrew.

About 40 State Department security agents arrived in Haiti on Friday amid allegations that Preval's personal security unit had been involved in the assassination of two right-wing politicians, and just after Preval's announcement that he was reorganizing his security force.

State Department officials have said they found evidence that members of Preval's security team were involved in the double assassination Aug. 20 of Pastor Antoine Leroy, the number-two official in the Mobilisation for National Development party (MDN), and MDN member Jacques Florival.

Preval told Reuters on Tuesday he had not been presented with hard evidence against his security personnel, but there was an investigation being carried out and the matter would be decided by Haitian judicial authorities.
Preval and Pettigrew met on Tuesday to discuss a possible extension of the mandate of the U.N. peacekeeping mission, of which Canadian soldiers are a majority.
Pettigrew said after the meeting that the Canadian government would be supportive of a request by the Haitian government to extend the peacekeeping mandate, which ends Nov. 30.
